title: Investor Library
head: name
line: The investors whose thinking shaped TEI: philosophy, principles, process and lessons.

items.name: Warren Buffett
items.philosophy: Buy exceptional businesses at reasonable prices and hold for the long term.
principles: Circle of Competence: only invest where you understand the business
Economic Moats: seek businesses with durable competitive advantages, such as brand, network effects, and pricing power
Owner Mentality: think like a business owner, not a trader
Compounding: allow great businesses and time to work together
items.mistake: Avoiding technology companies for too long.
items.lesson: A circle of competence should expand.
items.keyQuote: Price is what you pay. Value is what you get.

items.name: Charlie Munger
items.philosophy: Improve decision-making by building a broad understanding of reality.
principles: Latticework of Mental Models: use knowledge from multiple disciplines, such as psychology, economics, biology, and mathematics
Avoid Stupidity: a major advantage comes from avoiding obvious mistakes
Quality Over Quantity: a few exceptional decisions matter more than constant activity
items.lesson: The investor's biggest enemy is often themselves.
items.keyQuote: All I want to know is where I'm going to die so I'll never go there.

items.name: Benjamin Graham
items.philosophy: Invest based on fundamental value, not market emotion.
principles: Margin of Safety: buy with protection against being wrong
Mr Market: the market is emotional and irrational in the short term
Intrinsic Value: businesses have underlying economic worth
items.lesson: Pure statistical value investing became less suitable as exceptional businesses became more available.

items.name: Peter Lynch
items.investorType: Growth at a Reasonable Price Investor
items.philosophy: Individual investors can succeed by understanding businesses around them.
principles: Invest in What You Know: personal experience can create insight
Research Matters: a good story requires financial evidence
Avoid Following Crowds: understand the business yourself
items.lesson: A great company still requires understanding valuation.

items.name: Philip Fisher
items.philosophy: Invest in exceptional companies capable of long-term growth.
principles: Scuttlebutt Research: learn from customers, suppliers, competitors, and employees
Innovation: great companies continue improving
Long Holding Periods: avoid unnecessary selling

items.name: Howard Marks
items.philosophy: Successful investing requires understanding cycles and controlling risk.
principles: Second-Level Thinking: ask what everyone else believes, and whether it is already priced in
Risk Comes From Price: assets become risky when expectations become excessive
Cycles Repeat: human behaviour creates recurring patterns

items.name: Ray Dalio
items.philosophy: Build principles and systems that improve decision-making.
principles: Radical Truth: seek reality
Principles-Based Decision Making: create rules for recurring situations
Understand Economic Machines: study how economies function

items.name: Joel Greenblatt
items.philosophy: Simple rules can identify attractive investments.
principles: Magic Formula: combines business quality with attractive valuation

items.name: Stanley Druckenmiller
items.philosophy: Follow major trends while managing downside risk.
principles: Concentration: high conviction when opportunities are clear
Adaptability: change views when evidence changes
Risk Management: protect capital first

items.name: Terry Smith
items.philosophy: Buy good companies, do not overpay, do nothing.
principles: Focus on high returns on capital
Focus on strong businesses
Focus on long ownership

items.name: Nick Sleep
items.philosophy: Find exceptional businesses with long-term structural advantages.
principles: Focus on customer value creation
Focus on scale advantages
Focus on exceptional management

items.name: Jeff Bezos
items.philosophy: Build companies around customers and long-term thinking.
principles: Customer Obsession: start with customer needs
Long-Term Thinking: accept short-term sacrifice
Reinvestment: prioritise future opportunity
